subject: Request for additional evaluation credits — Kepler Labs
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@keplerlabs.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: extra eval credits for multi-team POC

Hi Jordan,

Quick ask — our teams (search, recommendations, infra) have been running concurrent POCs and we’ve burned through the evaluation credits you provided. We’re seeing good signal but need another batch of credits to complete cross-team benchmarks and a short spike test for throughput.

Is it possible to get a one-time boost (20k tokens) or separate eval buckets per team? We wanted to avoid interrupting the pilots while procurement sorts purchase orders. Happy to share more details on usage and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of ML Platform
Kepler Labs
attachments: kepler_signups_20270618.csv

Hi Aisha — thanks for the context. I can ask for a one-time top-up, but I need to run a quick internal check first (we’ve tightened approval after a few recent abuse cases). I’ve looped in Ben (sales ops) and Marissa (revops) to confirm the request and check the account footprint. Could you send the list of project emails and a short note on the expected token profile (per-hour/per-day)? That’ll speed approvals.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Fwd: Request: extra eval credits for multi-team POC

Forwarding Aisha's request — I pulled a quick usage snapshot and a signup correlation report (attached). Two quick flags:

- Several project emails map back to a small set of org domains and overlapping IP ranges over the last 10 days (see kepler_signups_20270618.csv).
- One email tied to the pilot appears to have created three separate accounts under the same domain with slight name variations, each requesting full eval credits.

I don’t want to block a legitimate expansion, but given recent coordinated trials we should treat this as a review rather than an automatic approval. Rishi — can you run the fraud heuristics and check if these signups are unique teams or scripted account creation? If clean, I’m happy to approve a limited top-up (10k tokens) and set per-team buckets. If suspicious, we should decline and propose a short paid pilot instead.

Attachments: kepler_signups_20270618.csv, kepler_trial_usage_snapshot.png

On 2027-06-18 10:02, Jordan Blake wrote:
> I can ask for a one-time top-up, but I need to run a quick internal check first (we’ve tightened approval after a few recent abuse cases).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: extra eval credits for multi-team POC

Summary of quick review:

- Signup fingerprinting shows 78% overlap in device fingerprint and 62% overlap in originating IPs across the apparently distinct accounts.
- Transactional patterns: identical usage bursts at near-aligned intervals (suspicious for scripted load testing).
- No matching corporate billing record in HubSpot (deal HS-87421 exists, but the contact set looks sparse).

Recommendation: deny the full open-top-up. Offer one of the following:
1) A constrained top-up (5k tokens) split into per-team buckets with stricter rate limits and a requirement to share project emails and PO reference before any further top-ups.
2) Offer discounted short-term paid pilot (30-day) that puts them on a metered invoice — sales can fast-track billing if procurement responds.

Ben/Jordan — if you want to proceed with option (1) I can mark the accounts as cleared with the rate-limits applied. If you prefer option (2) loop in Marissa to initiate an expedited procurement path.

Rishi
Trust & Safety Analyst | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: extra eval credits for multi-team POC

Hi Aisha — thanks for the quick patience while we ran an internal check. We want to support Kepler’s pilots, but our security team flagged some account overlap that looks like scripted creation rather than distinct project teams. To move forward quickly we can do one of the two options below:

Option A (fast, limited): We’ll provide a constrained top-up of 5,000 tokens divided into separate buckets for three project emails, with rate limits to prevent burst abuse. To enable this we’ll need confirmation of the three project leads’ corporate emails and an agreement to the temporary rate limits.

Option B (recommended for scale): We can start a 30-day paid pilot at a discounted rate and fast-track procurement — Marissa (copied) can help with PO templates and an expedited billing flow so you get predictable capacity for all teams.

If you can reply with which option you’d like and the project lead emails we’ll action it today. If your procurement team prefers to proceed, I can loop them in directly.

Best,
